audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 4 and 5 read Olaf/Skill/Olaf in both layers; the packet levelChart says Skill/Cho'Gath/Skill, the whys[] agree with the packet, and the mirror audit has ALREADY applied the packet chart from Cho'Gath's side.
audit.why: whys[3] 'Levels 4-5 are even' is a Skill row marked Olaf; whys[4] 'Cho owns level 6' is a Cho'Gath row marked Skill; whys[5] 'edges back even-to-favoured' is a Skill row marked Olaf. Leaving these would put the two directions in direct conflict and mirror-fix would overwrite them anyway.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 4, 5 set to Skill, Cho'Gath, Skill in BOTH layers as one atomic group, with ratings re-scaled. Rows 0, 1, 2, 6 already matched.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item stage was written as Olaf's fight-forcing spike; the packet and the mirror both call it parity. Level 6 was under-stated as merely 'reassess'.
audit.why: Feast (R, 80/70/60s) is the real spike in this lane and it arrives at 6. Olaf's first item does not out-run a Cho'Gath who is refilling max health with every successful Feast, which is why the mirror downgraded that stage to parity from the other side.
audit.corrected: phases[3], phases[4] and phases[5] rewritten to that timeline.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Ragnarok deletes CC' / 'R cleanses it too' appears in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, phases[4] and breakdown.late. Ragnarok grants IMMUNITY while active — it removes nothing already applied, so it has to be pressed before Rupture lands, not after. More importantly, the interaction that decides level 6 was only half-stated: Feast is TRUE damage, so the bonus armour and magic resist Ragnarok gives are worth exactly nothing against it.
audit.why: Riot text, Olaf R: 'passively gains increased armor and magic resist. He can activate this ability to become immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking.' Riot text, Cho'Gath R: 'Devours an enemy unit, dealing a high amount of true damage.' The kit file marks Feast trueDamage and percentHealth. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion from Cho'Gath's side.
audit.corrected: Cleanse language replaced with prevention-if-pressed-first; the true-damage-versus-resists point stated in phases[4], whys[4], spikes[1] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'W omnivamp' / 'W sustain' in whys[2], whys[3], spikes[1], mid and wants.you[1]. Olaf's W is Tough It Out — attack speed plus a shield, 16/15/14/13/12s, no healing.
audit.why: Riot text, Olaf W: 'Olaf's Attack Speed is increased and he gains a Shield.' The lifesteal is Berserker Rage (P), scaling with missing health. The mirror audit flagged the same five-field problem and could not reach mid and late inside the length band; both are corrected here.
audit.corrected: Shield and Berserker Rage named correctly in all five.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Rupture's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Even from 4: Feast stacks start absorbing your short trades, and the Tough It Out shield is what keeps it from tipping his way.

edits.before: Ragnarok deletes CC — once you press R, nothing he has stops the run-down. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Cho'Gath's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast is percent-HP TRUE damage, so Ragnarok's bonus armour and MR do nothing against it. Never all-in below half health at 6 — bait it first.

edits.before: Sundered Sky is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Rupture's cooldown.
edits.after: Even — Black Cleaver and Reckless Swing shred his stacking HP, but Feast refills it.

edits.before: - Cho'Gath Rupture: matchup-defining — Telegraphed. R cleanses it too. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Cho'Gath Rupture: matchup-defining — a telegraphed 6s knockup. Ragnarok prevents it, but only if pressed first. - Feral Scream: an 11s silence. - Your ultimate: kill windows only, never chip.

edits.before: Telegraphed. R cleanses it too. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Telegraphed, and back every 6s. Only engage once it is down or baited.

edits.before: Track Cho'Gath's Rupture (Knockup): Telegraphed. R cleanses it too. When it is down — Axe + E him.
edits.after: Track Rupture: a telegraphed 6s knockup. Ragnarok prevents it if pressed first — it never cleanses.

edits.before: Level 3 your E true damage burst lands clean through his bulk and W omnivamp heals the trade he can't match.
edits.after: Level 3 your E true damage lands clean through his bulk and the Tough It Out shield eats the answer back.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are even — his Feast stacks start absorbing your short trades, but your W sustain keeps it from tipping his way.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are even — his Feast stacks absorb your short trades, but Berserker Rage's lifesteal keeps it from tipping.

edits.before: Cho owns level 6: his R is true-damage percent-HP execute, so even with Ragnarok's CC immunity his ult finishes you when you're chunked.
edits.after: Cho owns level 6: Feast is percent-HP true damage, so Ragnarok's armour and MR count for nothing — it finishes you when you're chunked.

edits.before: Cho'Gath's R is a true-damage percent-HP execute — once you are chunked, his ult can finish you even through your W omnivamp, so this is his real kill window.
edits.after: Cho'Gath's R is percent-HP true damage — Ragnarok's bonus armour and MR are worth nothing against it, which is exactly why level 6 is his real kill window.

edits.before: Trade short with E true damage and W omnivamp so his W silence window is wasted
edits.after: Trade short with Reckless Swing and the W shield so his 11s Feral Scream is wasted

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay close to even because Cho starts farming Feast stacks and your short trades chip a growing HP pool, but you still out-sustain him with W omnivamp if you trade on his Q cooldown. Level 6 flips to him: Ragnarok ignores his knockup, but his R is true-damage percent execute, so the lower you dive the more his ult finishes you regardless of your immunity. Don't all-in below half HP at 6 — bait his W silence and R, then commit. After first item your Black Cleaver and E shred his stacks again and this is your strongest pressure window.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay close to even because Cho farms Feast stacks and your short trades chip a growing HP pool, but Berserker Rage's missing-health lifesteal holds you level if you trade on his 6s Q. Level 6 flips to him: Ragnarok stops the knockup, but Feast is percent-HP TRUE damage, so the armour and MR it grants are worth nothing — the lower you are, the more surely it finishes you. Don't all-in below half HP at 6; bait the 11s silence and the ult, then commit. After first item Cleaver and Reckless Swing shred his stacks again.

notes: Feral Scream is a silence, and a silence is a disable — so it can stop you casting Ragnarok, but cannot end an active one. The page's dosFull[2].t 'R to cleanse his Q knockup' is still wrong (Ragnarok prevents, never cleanses) but at 26 characters it sits on the applier's short-string boundary, so I left it rather than risk a skipped-but-counted edit; worth a manual fix. Cho'Gath's Q carries a derived 'grounding' flag Riot's description does not support (knockup, damage, slow); no grounding claim was made.
